arguments.sql_query:
WITH adv_ckd_concepts AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id IN (443612, 443611, 193782)
  UNION SELECT 443612 UNION SELECT 443611 UNION SELECT 193782
),
adv_ckd AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence
  WHERE condition_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM adv_ckd_concepts)
),
cv_categories AS (
  SELECT 'Hypertension' AS category, 316866 AS ancestor_id UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Heart failure', 316139 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Coronary/ischemic heart disease', 4185932 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Atrial fibrillation', 313217 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Cerebrovascular disease/stroke', 381591 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Peripheral vascular disease', 321052 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Myocardial infarction', 4329847
),
cv_concepts AS (
  SELECT category, descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM cv_categories cc
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = cc.ancestor_id
  UNION
  SELECT category, ancestor_id FROM cv_categories
),
counts AS (
  SELECT c.category, COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n
  FROM cv_categories c
  LEFT JOIN cv_concepts v ON v.category = c.category
  LEFT JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co
    ON co.condition_concept_id = v.concept_id
   AND co.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM adv_ckd)
  GROUP BY c.category
),
denom AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM adv_ckd)
SELECT c.category, c.n AS patients, d.total AS advanced_ckd_patients,
       CAST(100.0 * c.n / NULLIF(d.total,0) AS DECIMAL(5,1)) AS percent_of_advanced_ckd
FROM counts c CROSS JOIN denom d
ORDER BY c.n DESC;

Using the OMOP EHR cohort I found **43,394 patients with advanced CKD** (CKD stage 4/5 or ESRD concepts). Most frequent cardiovascular comorbidities were:

| Rank | Cardiovascular comorbidity | Patients | % of advanced CKD cohort |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Hypertension | 33,058 | 76.2% |
| 2 | Heart failure | 12,028 | 27.7% |
| 3 | Coronary/ischemic heart disease | 8,539 | 19.7% |
| 4 | Atrial fibrillation | 7,972 | 18.4% |
| 5 | Cerebrovascular disease/stroke | 7,580 | 17.5% |
| 6 | Peripheral vascular disease | 7,390 | 17.0% |
| 7 | Myocardial infarction | 6,263 | 14.4% |

Mechanistically, CKD-mineral bone disorder could link advanced CKD to these CVD phenotypes through:

- **Phosphate retention** → vascular smooth muscle osteogenic transformation → medial arterial calcification, arterial stiffness, coronary/PVD burden.
- **FGF23 elevation and Klotho deficiency** → left ventricular hypertrophy, myocardial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction; strong link to heart failure and arrhythmia risk.
- **Reduced calcitriol** → secondary hyperparathyroidism, RAAS/inflammatory activation, impaired vascular repair.
- **Secondary hyperparathyroidism** → calcium/phosphate mobilization, myocardial and vascular calcification, possible conduction/contractility effects.
- **High calcium-phosphate product** and calcium-based binders/positive calcium balance → accelerated vascular and valvular calcification.
- **Uremic inflammation/oxidative stress** amplifies mineral-driven calcification and atherosclerosis.

So, in this cohort, **hypertension dominates**, while **heart failure and atherosclerotic/vascular disease** are also common; phosphate–FGF23–Klotho–PTH dysregulation provides a plausible mineral-metabolism pathway connecting advanced CKD to vascular calcification, LV remodeling, and cardiovascular events.
